title: Understanding How Orthogonality of Parameters Improves Quantization of Neural Networks
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems 34(12), 10737–10746 (2023)
locator: Physical PDF pp. 1–9 (printed pp. 10737–10745): TQT introduced as the quantized retraining method, log-domain threshold training as described in [25], TQT baseline retraining, experiments with and without TQT (Fig. 1(c), Table I, Section V-C, Fig. 3) and the conclusion; bibliography p. 10 (printed p. 10746), reference [25]
version: Final IEEE TNNLS print, vol. 34, no. 12
summary: NVIDIA and Bilkent University researchers adopt TQT as their quantized retraining method, stating "we use TQT [25] as our baseline retraining method" (p. 5) and crediting it with "state-of-the-art results for several networks" (p. 1). They train thresholds in the log domain and follow the five-epoch schedule of [25], noting implementation differences (pp. 4–6), report accuracy before and after TQT (Table I, p. 6), contrast results without TQT (p. 7) and in the conclusion describe "a state-of-the-art TQT quantized retraining method" (p. 9).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Mixed Precision DNNs: All you need is a good parametrization
venue_basis: ICORE2026 A* venue; >100 Scholar citations; Uses or extends TQT
locator: PDF/printed pp. 1–2, 4–5, 8–9, introduction, quantizer constraints, experimental setup and TQT result rows; bibliography p. 10
version: Author-hosted arXiv copy bearing ICLR 2020 publication header
summary: Sony researchers implement TQT as the fixed-bitwidth benchmark for their mixed-precision method, learning qmax at a fixed 2-bit width "as was done in (Jain et al., 2019)" and reporting the "TQT" configuration in their CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tables (pp. 8–9). They credit Jain et al., in work parallel to their own, with learning the quantizer's dynamic range through the straight-through estimator (p. 2) and cite it for the power-of-two step size that efficient hardware requires (p. 4).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained uniform quantization for accurate and efficient neural network inference on fixed-point hardware.

title: A Reduced-Precision Network for Image Reconstruction
venue: ACM Transactions on Graphics 39(6), Article 231 (SIGGRAPH Asia 2020)
venue_basis: ICORE2026 A* venue; Uses or extends TQT
locator: Physical PDF pp. 3 and 6 (Section 5.1): trained quantization thresholds and log-space threshold training following Jain et al. [2019]; bibliography p. 11
version: ACM Transactions on Graphics publisher PDF
summary: University of California, Santa Cruz and Intel researchers adopt TQT's threshold training in the quantization of their 4-bit QW-Net image-reconstruction network, stating "Following Jain et al. [2019], we train the thresholds in log space" to improve stability with quantized training (Section 5.1, p. 6). The article explains that Jain et al. and Esser et al. showed that quantization thresholds could be trained to improve accuracy, with a straight-through-estimator gradient that lets thresholds grow for dynamic range or shrink for precision (p. 3). The log-space training is attributed to Jain et al. alone.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Optimizing the Deployment of Tiny Transformers on Low-Power MCUs
locator: Physical PDF p. 1 (printed p. 526), Section I: data quantization citation [3]; p. 6 (printed p. 531), Section IV-C: the uniform symmetric TQT quantizer used in the QuantLib flow; bibliography p. 15 (printed p. 540), reference [3]
version: Published IEEE Transactions on Computers print
summary: Researchers in the ETH Zürich/University of Bologna PULP group quantize their tiny transformers for low-power microcontrollers with TQT, stating "We use the uniform symmetric quantizer from the SotA [state-of-the-art] Trained Quantization Threshold (TQT) method [3]", and specify the functional behavior of the TQT quantizer in their deployment flow (Section IV-C, p. 6). The introduction also cites TQT for data quantization among standard hardware-agnostic optimization techniques (p. 1).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Integer-Only CNNs with 4 Bit Weights and Bit-Shift Quantization Scales at Full-Precision Accuracy
locator: PDF/printed pp. 2, 11–14, 17–20: Jain et al. [12] in the introduction, quantizer design, adopted training practices and TQT Table 2 results; bibliography p. 23, reference [12]
version: Published journal PDF from KU Leuven repository
summary: KU Leuven researchers take TQT as the starting point of their work: crediting Jain et al. with having "already proved" that 8-bit models with power-of-two scales reach full-precision accuracy, they set out to extend this to 4-bit weights (pp. 2, 14). They adopt its method, optimizing power-of-two scales "as proposed by Jain et al." (p. 12) with its quantizer, hyperparameters and scale freezing (p. 17), and extend its freezing to per-channel scales, finding its "per-layer results were consistent with ours" (p. 19). Table 2 lists TQT as the only prior power-of-two-scale method, within 1.6 points of full precision at 4-bit weights (p. 20).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: 7 μJ/inference end-to-end gesture recognition from dynamic vision sensor data using ternarized hybrid convolutional neural networks
locator: Physical PDF pp. 5–6, 9–10: TQT as one of two quantization-aware training algorithms, TQT hyperparameters and Table 4 TQT versus INQ results; bibliography p. 14, reference [67]
version: Published open-access journal PDF (Elsevier)
summary: ETH Zürich and University of Bologna researchers train their ternarized gesture-recognition networks with two quantization-aware training algorithms, INQ and TQT (p. 6). They use TQT to learn weight and activation clipping bounds (pp. 5–6), specify its hyperparameters (Table 3, p. 9) and train their Pareto-front networks with it (p. 9). They report that "the combination of ReLU activations and TQT yields the highest classification accuracy", ahead of INQ (Table 4, p. 10).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: A Resource Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only FPGA-Based CNN Accelerator for Real-Time Facial Emotion Recognition
locator: Physical PDF pp. 3–4, 6–7, 10–12: TQT in related work, LLTQ proposed to address the disadvantages of previous works including TQT and derived as an alternative to TQT's power-of-two scale mapping, Figure 3, the implemented TQT/LSQ/LLTQ comparison and its Table 1 TQT row; bibliography p. 15, reference [39]
version: IEEE Access open-access publisher PDF
summary: Inha University and Sangmyung University researchers identify TQT and LSQ as "the current state-of-the-art quantization methods" (p. 6) and develop log level threshold quantization (LLTQ) from TQT's power-of-two scale mapping: LLTQ maps the trainable parameter directly to a power-of-two scale and replaces TQT's pre-calibration with first-batch statistics (pp. 3–4, 6). They illustrate and train TQT, LSQ and LLTQ (pp. 7, 10) and report TQT as hardware-friendly but about 0.45% below floating-point accuracy, a gap LLTQ closes (pp. 11–12).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: A Low Memory Footprint Quantized Neural Network for Depth Completion of Very Sparse Time-of-Flight Depth Maps
locator: Physical PDF p. 2, Section 2.2 (printed p. 2687): QAT citation group including [23]; p. 5, Section 5.1 (printed p. 2690): uniform-precision QAT using learnable qmax as in TQT [23]; bibliography p. 9 (printed p. 2694), reference [23]

The related-work section cites TQT among recent quantization-aware training methods that "proved effective on classification tasks" (p. 2).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: QKD: Quantization-aware Knowledge Distillation
venue_basis: >100 Scholar citations; Uses or extends TQT
locator: Physical PDF pp. 2–3, 7, trainable intervals, dequantization and depthwise-layer sensitivity; bibliography p. 9, reference [17]
version: Reviewed arXiv manuscript
summary: Seoul National University and Qualcomm researchers state that TQT [17] and LSQ [8] "introduce uniform quantization using trainable interval values" and that "Our QKD leverages these trainable approaches in the baseline quantization implementation" (p. 2), introducing trainable interval parameters for each layer's weights and input activations similar to [8, 17, 45] (p. 3). They also cite TQT on the quantization sensitivity of depthwise convolutions (p. 7). Knowledge distillation is applied on top of this baseline, so the reported results reflect the combined method.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Improving Low-Precision Network Quantization via Bin Regularization
venue_basis: ICORE2026 A* venue; Uses or extends TQT
locator: Physical PDF p. 2 (printed p. 5242): related-work QAT citation group including [19]; p. 8 (printed p. 5248): Section 4.8 hardware-friendly baseline following [19, 21], Table 9 TQT, TQT+L2 and TQT+BR rows and the reported +3.7% over TQT; bibliography p. 9 (printed p. 5249), reference [19]
version: IEEE Xplore published print, ICCV 2021 proceedings
summary: Xilinx researchers in Beijing build bin regularization on a hardware-friendly quantization baseline that they re-implement following references [19, 21], where [19] is TQT: power-of-two step sizes, low-bit first and last layers, quantized inputs and outputs of element-wise additions, 8-bit biases and batch normalization merged during training (p. 8). Table 9 reports 63.8% top-1 accuracy for TQT, 65.8% for TQT+L2 and 67.5% for TQT+BR on 4-bit MobileNetV2, which the text describes as "+3.7% over TQT" (p. 8). The authors are affiliated with Xilinx Inc.; the entry is employer-linked.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained uniform quantization for accurate and efficient neural network inference on fixed-point hardware.

title: F8Net: Fixed-Point 8-bit Only Multiplication for Network Quantization
locator: Physical PDF pp. 2–3, 7–8: positioning against the power-of-two fixed-point scaling of Jain et al. (2019), contrast with directly trained fractional lengths and TQT rows in Table 1; bibliography p. 12
version: arXiv:2202.05239 PDF carrying the ICLR 2022 conference header
summary: Snap Inc., Northeastern University and Rice University researchers define F8Net against the fixed-point quantization of Jain et al. (2019), which uses trainable power-of-two scale factors to replace multiplication with bit shifting, stating that their work "differs from previous efforts (Jain et al., 2019) in three major aspects" (p. 2). They contrast F8Net's on-the-fly fractional length with TQT's directly trained fractional length (p. 7) and compare with TQT in Table 1 for MobileNet V1 and V2b, reporting that their approach gives better results (p. 8).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2019), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: INT8 Activation Ternary or Binary Weights Networks: Unifying Between INT8 and Lower-bit Width Quantization
venue: Journal of Robotics, Networking and Artificial Life 9(2) (2022), 171–176
locator: Physical PDF pp. 2–5: TQT as the INT8 method, activations quantized with TQT via Xilinx Brevitas, TQT-based settings and conclusion; bibliography p. 5, reference 11
version: Published journal PDF (J-STAGE)
summary: Kyushu Institute of Technology researchers quantize the activations of their ITBWN networks to INT8 with TQT while using binary or ternary weights (pp. 3–4). They describe TQT's removal of the zero point, its power-of-two scale and its threshold training with the straight-through estimator (p. 2), and report that INT8 activations from TQT or BinaryConnect allow the weight-quantized models to deploy without the cost of floating-point accumulation (p. 5). They use the default TQT implementation in Xilinx Brevitas, which they describe as having "minor differences with the TQT settings": no power-of-two scale and a different scale initialization (p. 3).
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.

title: Efficient SAR Vessel Detection for FPGA-Based On-Satellite Sensing
venue: SEC ’25, Tenth ACM/IEEE Symposium on Edge Computing (2025)
locator: Physical PDF p. 5, Section 3.2: INT8 Vitis AI quantization with power-of-two scaling and QAT using a straight-through estimator [35]; p. 11, Section 4.2.2, Table 4 and Section 4.3: QAT with a quantizer parameter learning rate and the deployed FPGA QAT models; bibliography p. 16, reference [35]
version: Published ACM version (open access, CC BY-NC 4.0)
summary: The Alan Turing Institute researchers deploy a YOLOv8-based SAR vessel detector on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA, quantizing it to INT8 with the Vitis AI Quantizer using symmetric power-of-two scaling; the sentence describing post-training quantization and quantization-aware training (QAT) "using a straight-through estimator" cites reference [35], the TQT paper (p. 5). They retrain with a tuned quantizer-parameter learning rate (Section 4.2.2) and report that the deployed QAT models match the expected GPU performance with little to no degradation (Table 4, Section 4.3, p. 11). The article does not state which Vitis AI QAT mode was used, and the use came through the AMD/Xilinx Vitis AI toolchain.
authorship_link: Jain, Gural, Wu and Dick (2020), Trained quantization thresholds for accurate and efficient fixed-point inference of deep neural networks.
